stem.en: A note gives a tiger's scientific name as "tigris" only. What is wrong with this note?

text.en: Nothing, since "tigris" alone is a complete scientific name.

feedback.en: A scientific name has two parts, so one word is not enough.

text.en: Leaving out a word moves the tiger into a new family.

feedback.en: The tiger stays in its family. The note is only incomplete.

text.en: It shows that the tiger does not have any genus.

feedback.en: The tiger has a genus, Panthera. The note has left it out.

text.en: It has no genus: the name is Panthera tigris.

feedback.en: Right. Both words together form the scientific name.

explanation.en: A scientific name has two parts, the genus and the species name. Both words are needed: Panthera tigris.

hints.en: How many parts does a scientific name have?
